one_liner: IPDPS 2022 artifact: optimized CUDA self-synchronizing and gap-array Huffman decoders, reported 3.64x faster than cuSZ's GPU Huffman decoder.
what_it_does: Four GPU Huffman decoders in separate directories: the original CUHD self-synchronization decoder (ICPP 2018), the original gap-array code (ICPP 2020), and optimized versions of both (opt-self-sync, opt-gap-array), the optimized ones built on the CUHD codebase. Each optimized decoder builds a demo binary or a static library (make lib, cuhd.a) exposing cuhd::CUHDGPUDecoder::decode() over CUHD's GPU input/output/codetable buffer classes, plus a sequential CPU length-limited Huffman encoder (llhuff). The run.sh scripts take cuSZ's quantization codes (cuSZ run with --skip huffman), encode them on the CPU, time GPU decoding, and runcusz.sh times cuSZ's own decompression as the baseline.
how_it_is_fast: Per the paper abstract (WebSearch snippet) and the code: decoded symbols are staged in shared memory and written to global memory from there, the shared-memory size is tuned online, memory access patterns are improved, and warp divergence is reduced. In opt-gap-array, an 8-bit gap per 4-unit (128-bit) subsequence removes the inter-block synchronization phase (phase 2 is empty); after an exclusive scan of per-subsequence symbol counts (Thrust), blocks are bucketed by compression ratio with a CUB radix sort and the final decode/write kernel is launched on 9 CUDA streams with shared buffers of 1,024 to 8,192 (or 3,584) 16-bit symbols per bucket. Lookup uses a 2^9-entry table cached in shared memory (cache_len 9).
when_to_use: GPU decompression in cuSZ-style error-bounded lossy compressors, where the Huffman stage decodes 16-bit quantization codes (1,024-symbol alphabet) on an NVIDIA GPU.
Building or benchmarking a GPU Huffman decoder: the repo puts both original decoders and both optimized ones behind the same harness on the same datasets.
When you control the encoder and can store an extra gap byte per 128 bits of compressed data (opt-gap-array), or need plain Huffman streams decoded on the GPU without format changes (opt-self-sync).
Large, mostly compressible inputs on Volta-class or newer GPUs, where decoding throughput rather than per-call latency matters.
when_not_to_use: Byte-oriented general-purpose compression or standard formats (Deflate, zstd, JPEG): symbols are 16-bit, codewords are capped at 14 bits, and the encoder is CUHD's own length-limited format.

Production pipelines: research artifact, 5 commits ending 2022-03-01, editor lock and backup files committed (.#cuhd_gpu_decoder.cu, #cuhd_gather.h#), no tests beyond the demo's equality check, and cuSZ integration is left to the user.
Small inputs or latency-sensitive calls: each decode() call allocates and frees its scratch buffers, runs a CUB sort and creates and destroys 9 CUDA streams.
Non-NVIDIA or non-Linux targets: CUDA with CUB/Thrust only, Makefiles hard-code sm_70 and /usr/local/cuda, and the host code uses -march=native.
If you need the orig-gap-array code under a license: that directory is the unlicensed Hiroshima University code and has no LICENSE file.

integration.dependencies: CUDA toolkit with Thrust and CUB; cuSZ (separate build) and the SDRBench datasets (getdata.sh, via wget from a Globus endpoint) only for the paper's benchmark
integration.min_toolchain: Tested with GCC 8.3.1 and NVCC 11.1 (README); Makefiles use -std=c++17 for host code and --std=c++14 for CUDA, arch sm_70 by default
integration.platforms: NVIDIA GPU (built for sm_70 by default; inherited CUHD README says compute capability 3.0+), Linux
integration.thread_safety: not documented; decode() keeps global timing arrays and an invocation counter, so concurrent calls are not safe
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it decodes the same cuSZ quantization codes, but the stream is encoded by its own CPU llhuff encoder (with a gap array for opt-gap-array), so cuSZ's Huffman format and code would have to be replaced, not linked against

gotchas: License is per directory: opt-self-sync, opt-gap-array and orig-self-sync carry LGPL-3.0 LICENSE files and CUHD headers ('released under LGPL-3.0'); the repo root and orig-gap-array have none.

The demo maps any input symbol above 1024 to 0 before encoding and then checks the decoded output against that altered buffer, so arbitrary 16-bit files are silently changed (fine for cuSZ codes, not for general data).
The demo's first 'throughput' line divides by wall time of the whole decode() call including allocations; the second sums per-phase times; both use 1024^3, so 'GB/s' is GiB/s.

opt-self-sync/run.sh and opt-gap-array/run.sh are identical (both print 'best solution + self-synchronization'), CUSZ_DIR and DATA_DIR are empty and must be filled in, and $shared_size is never set, so tuning is always online.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over CUHD/gpuhd and Huffman_coding_Gap_arrays when you want the fastest of these GPU Huffman decoders for 16-bit quantization codes: it contains both and reports beating them as well as cuSZ. Pick FiniteStateEntropy's huff0 or PIVCO-Huffman for CPU byte-stream decoding, and multians or Recoil if you can switch from Huffman to ANS.
verified_claims_summary: Per WebSearch snippets of the IPDPS 2022 abstract (paper not opened; arXiv, IEEE and NSF pages blocked), on an NVIDIA Tesla V100 32 GB with an unnamed x86_64 host, GCC 8.3.1 and NVCC 11.1 (-O3, sm_70), the optimized decoders averaged 3.64x faster Huffman decoding than cuSZ's native GPU decoder and 2.43x faster overall cuSZ decompression across eight scientific datasets (the repo's scripts run five: HACC, EXAALT, CESM, Nyx, Isabel, error bound 1e-3). A further snippet says shared-memory sizing alone moves throughput between 158 and 233 GB/s; the repo itself publishes no numbers.
status_note: Abandoned research artifact (last commit 2022-03-01, 3 stars); the optimized decoders are LGPL-3.0 per their directory LICENSE files, so they can be reused under copyleft terms, while orig-gap-array is unlicensed.
sources_read: WebSearch: "Optimizing Huffman Decoding for Error-Bounded Lossy Compression on GPUs" shared memory compression ratio gap array self-synchronization GB/s V100 (snippets only)
